# OntoKin goal

The owner refined the October 28 mission on November 9, 2026 after reviewing *OntoKin in the Age of AI-Generated 3D*. Current results are recorded in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md). Repository coordination follows [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Mission

Build OntoKin as a typed semantic and physical intermediate language for AI agents. An agent should be able to describe what an object is, inspect how its parts connect and move, change one instance, validate that change, and regenerate the object for a named destination. The accepted `.ok` revision owns the design intent. Classes, instances, functions and reusable libraries give that intent a programmable form that people can review. Ordinary execution must continue without a model call per frame.

Take a wheel mounted on a robot. Its visual mesh may come from an artist, an image-conditioned generator or a CAD kernel. The program should name the wheel, give its radius and mass in declared units, identify the axle frame and specify allowed rotation. An agent replacing the mesh must still verify dimensions, attachment and motion. For an external asset, the proposed workflow is to pin its origin and bytes, fit it to the declared frame and check the mapping. A photograph or Gaussian-splat capture can supply scenery. A physical claim about that scene needs independently measured engineering geometry or a validated collision proxy.

## Near-term investment

Fund features that help an agent complete a measured physical-asset task. Concentrate on five capabilities.

| Capability | What the agent must be able to demonstrate |
| --- | --- |
| Semantic assemblies | Address an instance by a stable identity, reuse its class and preserve the identities of its siblings. |
| Dimensions and constraints | Check quantities in declared units and frames, and locate a violated constraint in source or delivered geometry. |
| Physical relationships | Distinguish part ownership, spatial following and mechanical connection. Identify the authority for each motion and check the relevant range or physical result. |
| Targeted repair | Inspect a failure, apply an atomic edit to the accepted source, and show that an invalid edit preserved the last accepted revision and an intended edit preserved unrelated parts. |
| Multi-backend delivery | Map the same source revision to named destination profiles. Verify which identities, dimensions, joint properties and motions survive each mapping and report any loss. |

Delegate mesh synthesis, precision solid modeling, rendering and general-purpose simulation to specialist tools where a task needs them. Keep the reference implementation and its bounded physical profiles for reproducible checks. New language or engine work should address a demonstrated authoring failure or an essential validation need. Defer a general importer, capture pipeline or new production backend until the comparison below justifies the expense.

Recorded GLB (binary glTF) is the current delivery path. Candidate destinations include Blender for visualization, OpenUSD Physics for bodies and joints, Unreal for engine delivery, and a CAD kernel for representable solids. A proposed adapter needs a versioned mapping and a test in the receiving application. Reopen the actual output, measure geometry and playback where applicable, and exercise any claimed live behavior. Record unsupported features explicitly. The [export and validation contract](docs/engineering/OK-ENG-002-3d-scene-animation-export-and-visual-validation.md) distinguishes delivery from destination evidence.

## How to decide whether to expand

**Can the same agent make reliable, localized repairs and reuse the result more effectively with OntoKin than with direct Blender/Python?** The [cart trial](docs/engineering/external-environment-c177/README.md) established a source-edit and clearance check. The [rotary-indexer pilot](docs/engineering/rotary-indexer-c179/README.md) is the first held-out paired task. Preserve its frozen prompts, run order, two native exporters, common GLB checker and viewer. Start only after an isolated controller demonstrates the wall-clock and token cutoffs. Score the deliveries before revealing their routes.

If that pilot supports further study, target **30–50 unseen physical-asset tasks** with localized edits and later reuse. C177 sketched a cohort of 10–20 objects. Count distinct assemblies separately from tasks, and include variations across task families. Before runs, freeze the prompts, allowable preparation, success criteria, acceptable tolerances and the improvement large enough to justify continued investment. Give both routes the same model snapshot, settings, information, tools for inspection, resources and output requirements. In a study intended to isolate the language's contribution, use the same versioned Blender backend for both routes. Qualify that OntoKin adapter first. The existing pilot compares complete native workflows with a shared evaluator.

Record first-pass acceptance, invalid intermediate states, model and repair turns, token use, elapsed time and human interventions. On the actual deliveries, measure dimensions, unchanged siblings, prescribed motion or physical outcomes as applicable, clean regeneration and success on a later localized edit. Report paired successes and failures across all tasks. Compare cost at matched success levels and separate reusable setup from task-specific work.

Expand only where the measured improvement meets the predeclared criterion. A mixed result should narrow investment to the task families or semantics that earned their cost. If direct tooling performs as well or better, pause broad language and backend expansion. One successful repair can qualify a workflow for further study. It cannot establish a general authoring advantage. [C180 comparison design and decision record](docs/engineering/semantic-physical-scope-c180/README.md)

# Working on OntoKin

The owner authorizes autonomous technical development and repository stewardship toward [GOAL.md](GOAL.md). Routine work within that mandate should continue through implementation, verification, and reviewable publication. This is not legal ownership and does not enlarge platform permissions or authorization outside the project.

## Recenter and resume

At the start of a session, after compaction, and before choosing or closing a milestone:

1. Read GOAL and [STATUS.md](STATUS.md). Restate the current goal and the next unmet acceptance gate to yourself.
2. Inspect repository status/tree, the actual GitHub head, the integration lease, and relevant CI. Do not treat a synthetic local snapshot commit as the remote head or discard existing work.
3. Read the relevant specifications through [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), especially the adopted language rules and the active engineering contract. Historical proposals are not current implementation guarantees.
4. Continue authorized useful work. Record genuine blockers and the concrete next action; do not silently replace the goal with an easier demonstration.

## Coordinate parallel workers and main integration

**Parallel branch development is allowed; main integration remains serialized.** A live integration lease is **not** a project-wide read-only lock. It protects writes to `main`, integration ownership in `STATUS.md`, and any explicitly reserved overlapping/shared files. Independent workers (including scheduled reviewers that have actual editing tools) may implement, test, and publish **nonoverlapping** work on their **own** branches while someone else integrates. An enabled schedule or branch is not proof that multiple agents are executing.

## Source ownership and admitted model

An immutable UTF-8 `.ok` revision owns geometry, colors, local frames, attachment,
two masses, four contact-box dimensions and offsets, feeds, initial state,
collision enablement and left-stop placement. No external imports or assets are
allowed. Its dependency closure is the exact adopted grammar, schemas and
backend mapping; each file is SHA-256 identified. Generated Python maps these
declarations and never supplies an undeclared geometric or physical design
constant. Source SHA-256 and closure hashes accompany every attempt.

The scene contains exactly these stable visible-part keys: `base`,
`left_carriage`, `left_shoe`, `left_stop`, `right_carriage`, `right_shoe`,
`right_stop`. Names preceding `@` are labels; rename and declaration reorder
have no effect on semantic identity or mapping. Every declaration key is unique
across part/body/collider/follow namespaces. Native names and GLB node names use
stable keys. Occurrence identity is `(module_key, scene_key, declaration_key)`;
revision identity is recorded separately. A label or source-line change cannot
reattach a collider.

`part` declares `box`, `color`, `rotation`, and, for a root part, `at`. Box and
placement vectors have unit `[mm]`; color is unitless linear RGBA; quaternion is
unitless `[w,x,y,z]`. Geometry has a minimum-corner source origin. A followed
shoe has no independent `at` field. `follow` declares `parent`, `child`,
`offset[mm]` and identity `rotation`. This relationship is a massless, rigid
spatial attachment only. It supplies no force-bearing joint. Each shoe has one
follow parent, its matching carriage, and no body declaration.

`body` declares `part`, `mass[kg]`, `authority`, `guide`, `feed[mm/s]` and
`initial_velocity[mm/s]`. Only the two matching carriage bodies exist, with
stable IDs `body.left` and `body.right`, mass 1 kg each, `authority="solver"`,
`guide="world_x"`, initial velocity `[0,0,0]`, feeds 125 and 150 mm/s respectively.

def mesh_box(name, box_mm):
    x, y, z = [value / 2 for value in box_mm]
    corners = [(-x, -y, -z), (x, -y, -z), (x, y, -z), (-x, y, -z),
               (-x, -y, z), (x, -y, z), (x, y, z), (-x, y, z)]
    faces = [(0, 3, 2, 1), (4, 5, 6, 7), (0, 1, 5, 4),
             (3, 7, 6, 2), (0, 4, 7, 3), (1, 2, 6, 5)]
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name + "_mesh")
    mesh.from_pydata([native_point(corner) for corner in corners], [], faces)
    mesh.update()
    return mesh

The writer emits one glTF 2.0 scene and one animation clip in a GLB version 2 container. Its JSON and embedded binary chunks use the required alignment. Geometry uses indexed triangles with float32 positions/normals and unsigned 16- or 32-bit indices. All nodes have translation and rotation channels sharing one float32 time accessor. No external asset URI, required extension, skin, or live physics payload is needed for this profile. These choices define the adapter's narrow output subset. [G1]

Global source and relationship metadata lives at `extras.ontokin`. Each node's `extras.ontokin` identifies its source occurrence or helper role. Animation metadata retains exact sampled and boundary times. Geometry buffers and materials can be shared while each object retains its own node identity and tracks. The bounded reader in `ontokin.gltf` checks this specific layout; it is not a general-purpose glTF importer or a replacement for the Khronos validator.

| Source feature | `ontokin.glb/0.1` treatment | What the destination receives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spheres and boxes | Converted to meshes; sphere curvature approximated | Visible rigid polygon surfaces with recorded construction settings. |
| Empty geometry | Retained as an object identity without an authored surface | An inspectable node; an optional separately marked display helper. |
| Object occurrence identity | Preserved in metadata | Mapping from an output node back to the source occurrence. |
| Source ownership and relationships | Preserved as metadata; spatial hierarchy flattened | Inspectable records, without executable mechanical constraints. |
| Evaluated positions and orientations | Baked to sampled tracks | Playback within the measured output tolerances. |
| Concurrent actions, holding, and release | Baked to their combined evaluated result | One authoritative recorded pose per object at each sample. |
| Gravity and physical body descriptions | Evaluated by OntoKin; relevant assumptions retained as metadata | Recorded motion and traceability, without a destination physics simulation. |
| RGBA appearance | Converted to a basic display material | Authored color/alpha plus disclosed exporter shading defaults. |
| Classes, pure methods, parameters, and action definitions | Remain authoritative in `.ok` | The GLB is a derived result, not a round-trip source editor. |
| Textures, skins, morph targets, collisions, general dynamic joints, and live controllers | Outside this profile | No implicit approximation or claim of destination support. |

The JSON report uses schema `ontokin.glb-report/0.1` and identifies the target contract separately. Its `source`, `scene`, `sampling`, `tolerances`, `representation`, `geometry`, `retention`, and `budgets` sections expose the corresponding decisions. The `retention` section distinguishes preserved metadata, baked motion, semantics that are not executable in the GLB, known conversion losses, helpers, and any source interval intentionally excluded by `--end`. Source syntax, callable definitions, source spans, complete site definitions, and source action/event arguments are not embedded for program reconstruction. The `.ok` must supply them.

Output identity and decoded numerical observations identify the checked artifact. The report also records the exporter version, Python/operating-system environment, and `source_code_sha256` over the sorted `ontokin/*.py` filenames and exact bytes, using the existing conformance report's hashing convention. This implementation digest is distinct from both the authored program's revision and the output GLB hash. A warning about an allowed presentation conversion is distinct from a blocking unsupported capability or exceeded tolerance.

Explicit export authorizes the recorded-pose conversion described here. It does not authorize silently substituting recorded playback when a user requests live destination physics, new interactive input, a skeletal rig, or a feature outside this profile. Such a request needs its own supported contract.

Metadata can help a downstream tool find an OntoKin source object, but an arbitrary importer may discard application-specific metadata. The authoritative `.ok` must remain available alongside the derived file when further editing or source delivery is required. A successful GLB write does not prove that another tool preserved the mapping after editing and re-export.

def __init__(self, path, ids):
        raw = Path(path).read_bytes()
        require(len(raw) >= 28 and struct.unpack_from("<4sII", raw) == (b"glTF", 2, len(raw)),
                "invalid GLB header")
        size, tag = struct.unpack_from("<I4s", raw, 12)
        require(tag == b"JSON" and size % 4 == 0 and 28+size <= len(raw), "invalid JSON chunk")
        self.doc = d = json.loads(raw[20:20+size])
        def check_extensions(x):
            if isinstance(x, dict):
                require(not x.get("extensions"), "extension payload outside core glTF profile")
                for k, v in x.items():
                    if k not in ("extras", "extensions"):
                        check_extensions(v)
            elif isinstance(x, list):
                for v in x:
                    check_extensions(v)
        check_extensions(d)
        blob_size, tag = struct.unpack_from("<I4s", raw, 20+size)
        require(tag == b"BIN\0" and blob_size % 4 == 0 and 28+size+blob_size == len(raw), "invalid BIN chunk")
        self.bin = raw[28+size:]
        require(d["asset"]["version"] == "2.0" and not d.get("extensionsRequired"),
                "unsupported required extension or glTF version")
        require(len(d["buffers"]) == 1 and "uri" not in d["buffers"][0]
                and 0 <= blob_size - d["buffers"][0]["byteLength"] <= 3, "expected one embedded buffer")
        require(len(d["scenes"]) == 1, "expected exactly one scene")
        require(not any(d.get(k) for k in ("skins", "images", "textures")),
                "skins and textures outside solid rigid profile")
        self.nodes = d["nodes"]
        roots = at(d["scenes"], d.get("scene", 0))["nodes"]
        self.parent, self.order, self.parts, self.tracks = {}, [], {}, {}

        def visit(i, parent):
            n = at(self.nodes, i)
            require(i not in self.parent, "cycle or shared child in scene")
            self.parent[i] = parent
            self.order.append(i)
            require("skin" not in n and "weights" not in n and not n.get("extensions"),
                    "unsupported skin, morph or node extension")
            if "mesh" in n:
                mesh = at(d["meshes"], n["mesh"])
                name = n.get("name")
                require(name in ids and mesh.get("name") == name,
                        f"mesh node and mesh must share the specified ID: {name!r} / {mesh.get('name')!r}")
                require(name not in self.parts, "part ID occurs on multiple mesh nodes")
                self.parts[name] = (i, *self.geometry(mesh))
            for child in n.get("children", []):
                visit(child, i)

        for i in roots:
            visit(i, None)
        require(set(self.parts) == ids, "missing semantic part")
        require(len(self.parent) == len(self.nodes), "unreachable node outside the default scene")
        for name in ids:
            require(sum(n.get("name") == name for n in self.nodes) == 1,
                    f"duplicate stable node ID: {name}")
        require(len(d["meshes"]) == len(ids), "unreferenced or extra mesh")
        for name in ids:
            require(sum(m.get("name") == name for m in d["meshes"]) == 1,
                    f"duplicate stable mesh ID: {name}")
        require(len(d["animations"]) == 1, "expected exactly one animation")
        anim = d["animations"][0]
        times = []
        for chan in anim["channels"]:
            i, path = chan["target"]["node"], chan["target"]["path"]
            require(i in self.parent and path in ("rotation", "translation", "scale")
                    and "matrix" not in self.nodes[i] and (i, path) not in self.tracks,
                    "unsupported or duplicate animation target")
            s = at(anim["samplers"], chan["sampler"])
            require(s.get("interpolation", "LINEAR") == "LINEAR", "unsupported interpolation")
            t = self.access(s["input"], "SCALAR", (5126,))[:, 0]
            require(len(t) and (np.diff(t) > 0).all() and t[0] >= 0 and t[-1] <= 2,
                    "invalid time range or key order")
            v = self.access(s["output"], "VEC4" if path == "rotation" else "VEC3", (5126,))
            require(len(v) == len(t), "inconsistent animation key counts")
            if path == "rotation":
                v = normalize_quats(v)
                # q and -q describe the same rotation and slerp takes the short arc.
                same = np.all(v == v[0], axis=1) | np.all(v == -v[0], axis=1)
                require(same.all(), "time-varying rotation outside translation-only profile")
                v[:] = v[0]
            if path == "scale":
                require((v == v[0]).all(), "time-varying scale is outside the rigid profile")
            self.tracks[i, path] = t, v
            times.extend(t)
        require(times and min(times) == 0 and max(times) == 2, "clip does not span [0,2] seconds")

def geometry(self, mesh):
        triangles, colors = [], []
        require(not mesh.get("weights") and not mesh.get("extensions"), "morphed or extended mesh")
        for p in mesh["primitives"]:
            require(p.get("mode", 4) == 4 and not p.get("targets") and not p.get("extensions")

            pos = self.access(p["attributes"]["POSITION"], "VEC3", (5126,))
            ix = (self.access(p["indices"], "SCALAR", (5121, 5123, 5125))[:, 0]
                  if "indices" in p else np.arange(len(pos)))
            require(len(ix) > 0 and len(ix) % 3 == 0 and ix.max() < len(pos), "invalid triangle indices")
            triangles.append(pos[ix].reshape(-1, 3, 3))
            m = at(self.doc["materials"], p["material"])
            pbr = m.get("pbrMetallicRoughness", {})
            rgb = finite(pbr.get("baseColorFactor", [1]*4), (4,))
            require("baseColorTexture" not in pbr and np.all((rgb >= 0) & (rgb <= 1)) and not m.get("extensions") and
                    m.get("alphaMode", "OPAQUE") == "OPAQUE" and rgb[3] == 1,
                    "unsupported non-solid material")
            colors.append(rgb[:3])
        require(bool(triangles), "empty visible mesh")
        return np.concatenate(triangles), np.array(colors)

def transforms(self, times):
        world, local = {}, {}
        for i in self.order:
            n = self.nodes[i]
            if "matrix" in n:
                require(not any(k in n for k in ("rotation", "scale", "translation")), "matrix and TRS mixed")
                mat = finite(n["matrix"], (16,)).reshape(4, 4).T
                require(np.array_equal(mat[3], [0, 0, 0, 1]), "non-affine node matrix")
                m = np.broadcast_to(mat, (len(times), 4, 4))
            else:
                m = np.zeros((len(times), 4, 4))
                m[:, 3, 3] = 1
                m[:, :3, 3] = self.track(i, "translation", times)
                m[:, :3, :3] = quaternion_matrix(self.track(i, "rotation", times)) * self.track(i, "scale", times)[:, None, :]
            parent = self.parent[i]
            local[i] = m
            world[i] = world[parent] @ m if parent is not None else m
        return world, local
